stages.title: Design Engine: site-wide design, families and proposals
stages.desc: Site-wide design decisions in Studio with contrast safety, section families with typed slots, and a generated design manifest with validated change proposals. Necessary work is driven by real sites; the AI experiment comes last.
stages.milestone: DE1: density, shape, heading style, motion level and section panels set once for the whole site, with contrast that explains itself (216–218, 168, 194). DE2: the split and hero families with shared slots (219, 193, 213). DE3: a generated design manifest and validated change proposals (215, 219, 220), then the design-reference experiment (221).

stages.title: Content Intelligence: correct structured data, explainable audits
stages.desc: One entity graph with stable @ids and tested visible-content parity, a page audit that returns evidence-backed findings, improvement records, then Search Console evidence. No scores; nothing publishes automatically.
stages.milestone: CI1: one structured-data module with stable @ids and typed parity (188, 191, 222, then 192 and 212 when a site needs them). CI2: page audit, fact rules, improvement records and AI crawler controls (223–225, 228, 195). CI3: search evidence from a real site: Search Console (226, then 202 and 210 in FX) and the AI-search evidence spike (229).

tasks.t: Design manifest generated from the schemas
tasks.what: design-manifest.generated.json built by npm run typegen from the section schemas, sectionStyle options, presets, layout rules, slots and the client-editable registry, with only purpose and example added by hand; CI fails when it is stale.
tasks.why: Tools and future AI need a reliable description of what the Design Engine supports, without a second source of truth.

tasks.t: Design settings v2: density, shape and heading style
tasks.what: Brand colours gains Density, Shape and Heading style as picture choices that render as :root CSS variables through resolveDesignTokens; unset keeps today's look, sections that set their own spacing keep it and are listed.
tasks.why: "More breathing room", "softer corners" and "more editorial headings" should be one change for the whole site, not code.

tasks.t: Site motion level, with a calmer setting on phones
tasks.what: Design settings gains Motion (Calm, Standard, Expressive) and On phones (Same, Calmer, Off), multiplied into every section's animation and parallax without a new provider or request; reduced motion still wins.
tasks.why: "Reduce the animation on mobile" is a site decision, not 30 section edits.

tasks.t: Glass and solid panels for any section
tasks.what: A Panel option in every section's Design tab (None, Glass, Solid card): glass over any suitable background, tinted with no blur over solid tones and frosted only where something varied is behind it, exact or guaranteed-bound contrast, and an automatic solid fallback with a warning that says what to fix.
tasks.why: "Make this section glass" is the most requested treatment and today exists only inside the Link list.

tasks.t: Shared slot registry (from the hero slot), with a video block
tasks.what: The hero's supporting-slot registry becomes a shared registry any section family can use (schema, component, where allowed, client-editable), the hero renders identically, and a video block joins stats, logos and badges.
tasks.why: "Add a video under the image" needs typed slots shared across families, not a new field per section.

tasks.t: Change proposals: contract, validator and draft applier (no AI)
tasks.what: A ChangeProposal format with npm run proposal validate and apply: checked against the manifest, Sanity validation, contrast and the client-editable registry, then written only as drafts (or one release) with revision guards, to scratch datasets.
tasks.why: Scripted and future AI-made changes must be validated, previewable and undoable before anyone publishes them.

tasks.t: Experiment: design reference to a validated proposal
tasks.what: Three real references turned into proposals (design decisions, sections, a gap list) in a Claude Code session, applied to a scratch dataset, corrected by hand and timed against a manual build; stop if correction exceeds 70% of manual time.
tasks.why: Tests whether design-reference import is worth building, with evidence instead of promises.

tasks.what: Every JSON-LD builder moves into src/lib/structured-data/ with document-keyed @ids that survive slug changes, a WebPage node on every page, authors linked to Person nodes where the 191 note allows, and typed, provenance-based parity in place of literal string matching.
tasks.why: Services and locations will add more markup; one module prevents contradictory or duplicated entities.

tasks.what: npm run audit:page returns findings in one shared contract (rule, basis, severity, evidence, why, fix with a Studio link, how to re-check), reusing launch:check, content health and the JSON-LD parity helper; Content health items carry the same rule IDs.
tasks.why: Answers "what is wrong with this page, why, and where do I fix it" with evidence instead of a score.

tasks.what: An agency-only improvement document type and a Record improvement action that captures the finding, before and after values, the published revision and a review date; the health issue lists records due for review.
tasks.why: "Did the improvement work?" needs a record of what changed, when and why.

tasks.what: Deterministic rules in the shared library: phone, email, ABN or address in page text that differs from Business info, stale facts, duplicate titles and summaries, and incomplete service and location pages once those types exist.
tasks.why: Contradictory facts are objective errors that confuse visitors and search engines, and they can be found without AI.

tasks.t: Spike: Search Console evidence for one real site
tasks.what: A read-only local import of 28 days of Search Console data (final, paged, truncation flagged) into a git-ignored folder, URL-to-document mapping, and CTR-gap and declining-page findings with caveats (AI Overviews and AI Mode impressions can't be separated through the API), written up for tasks 202 and 210.
tasks.why: Tests the evidence model on real data before Foundation's Search Health is built.

tasks.what: A declarative registry of what each feature needs (settings, kind, where set, never values), readiness from the existing config functions, npm run config:check, per-feature readiness in /api/site-info, health-workflow setup diagnostics and a generated README environment table.
tasks.why: Missing configuration should be found before launch, in plain English; it is the foundation of the Settings and Configuration Manager.

tasks.t: AI crawler controls: training separate from search
tasks.what: Two Site identity switches, AI training and AI search answers, with user agents grouped by purpose as the vendors document them, llms.txt following the search switch, and a migration that keeps every site's current behaviour.
tasks.why: Today opting out of AI training also removes a site from Perplexity's answers, and OpenAI's and Anthropic's search crawlers are not listed.

tasks.t: Spike: AI-search evidence for one real site
tasks.what: Manual exports from Search Console's generative AI report and Bing AI Performance, AI referrals from analytics and crawler fetches, joined with page-audit findings into evidence-backed findings (no score), written up with a recommendation for Foundation.
tasks.why: Tests whether the AI-search signals that exist today are actionable before anything is built to import them.
